blogs.title: When B12 Deficiency Isn’t the Whole Story: Pancytopenia with Premature Ageing Clues
blogs.description: This post would examine the diagnostic danger of stopping at a correct but incomplete diagnosis. Using this case, it would show how severe vitamin B12 deficiency can explain dimorphic anaemia, hypersegmented neutrophils and ineffective erythropoiesis, yet fail to account for premature greying, pulmonary fibrosis, hepatic fibrosis and persistent multisystem disease. The focus would be on recognizing ‘red flags beyond nutrition’ in young adults with pancytopenia.

blogs.title: A Positive DAT Does Not Equal Autoimmune Haemolysis
blogs.description: This post would explore the common bedside dilemma of interpreting a positive direct antiglobulin test in a patient with anaemia. It would contrast autoimmune haemolysis with ineffective erythropoiesis by emphasizing the low reticulocyte count, marrow erythroid hyperplasia, indirect hyperbilirubinaemia and elevated LDH seen in megaloblastic states. The teaching point is how to avoid overcalling immune haemolysis when the physiology points toward intramedullary destruction.

blogs.title: Young, Fibrotic, and Unexplained: When Liver Plus Lung Disease Should Trigger a Telomere Workup
blogs.description: This post would focus on the under-recognized phenotype of telomere biology disorders presenting outside the classic dyskeratosis congenita triad. It would discuss why the combination of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, cirrhosis or hepatic fibrosis, cytopenias and subtle premature-ageing features in a young adult should prompt consideration of a telomere syndrome. The broader message is that combined organ fibrosis is often the biggest clue to an inherited telomere disorder.

blogs.title: PARN and the Problem of the VUS: How to Use Genotype-Phenotype Correlation in Real Patients
blogs.description: This post would tackle the practical challenge of a monoallelic PARN variant classified as a variant of uncertain significance. Rather than treating a VUS as either meaningless or definitive, it would show how clinicians can integrate gene function, domain-level biology, ACMG criteria, prior literature and the patient’s phenotype to support a working diagnosis. It would also highlight the role of confirmatory telomere-length testing and careful documentation when genetics outpaces certainty.

blogs.title: Why the Diagnosis Changes Everything: Management Pearls in Telomere Biology Disorders
blogs.description: This post would review why identifying a telomere biology disorder matters even when treatment is largely supportive. Topics would include surveillance for marrow failure, pulmonary and hepatic progression, malignancy risk, family counselling, and the special implications for haematopoietic stem cell transplantation in inherited marrow disease. It would also discuss emerging but still unsettled therapies such as androgen-based telomere support and the importance of multidisciplinary follow-up.
